newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Nervous market keeps dlr/yen vols pumped.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Nervous market keeps dlr/yen vols pumped.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options remained strongly supported in U.S. dealings Wednesday as market participants continued to fear another sudden downdraft in the spot currency, options traders said.

Although the dollar has come back from an early dip below 113, worry that it could take another swipe at 110 yen after brushing against the level last week has traders edgy and reluctant to sell options, especially short dates, they said.
Demand for downside strikes continues after buying interest in low-strike yen calls intensified Monday when the dollar broke below 114 yen, dealers said.
But several traders said activity had quieted as the spot held its ground and the market looked toward Thursday's U.S. April trade data and the G7 summit this weekend in Denver.
"People in yen are concerned about the trade figures tomorrow. The interesting thing is it is concentrated in dollar/yen and not moving into the other dollars," said a U.S. bank trader in New York.
Talk circulated that a $2 billion one-year option traded in the 104.50 strike on Tuesday and was responsible for keeping dollar/yen volatilities inflated across the curve.
"It takes a long time for a deal like that to work its way through the market," the New York trader said.
In addition, traders said Japanese corporations were showing interest in buying 110 yen calls to protect long dollar positions.
Risk reversals, the put-call pricing differential, stayed sharply skewed for yen calls at about 2.1/2.55 after pushing above 2.0 on Tuesday.
One-month volatility was 13.1/13.4 percent, up 0.3 point from late in the previous session, and one-year was 11.0/11.2 percent, up 0.2 point.
In dollar/mark, the volatility curve has moved to a gentle upward slope from essentially flat last week, implying investors have a longer-term risk horizon, the U.S. bank trader said.
"People don't think that much is going to happen in the near term," he said.
One-month volatility fell 0.2 point to 9.0/9.3 percent while one-year held steady at 9.3/9.6 percent.

A New York dealer at a Japanese bank said although the focus of the market is dollar/yen, the bullish yen bias was also being felt in mark/yen, where risk reversals were skewed 1.3/1.5 heavily in favor of mark puts.
